description: Computes when the EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) Article 14 reports are due after an actively exploited vulnerability or a severe incident: the 24-hour early warning, the 72-hour notification and the final report, and who receives them (the coordinating CSIRT and ENISA). Takes the event type and the time the manufacturer became aware (ISO 8601 with zone), optionally when a fix became available or when the 72-hour notification was sent. Returns each due time in UTC with its article and how to submit on ENISA's Single Reporting Platform. For what each report must contain: cra_report_draft. Does not cover GDPR or NIS2 breach deadlines and does not decide whether an event must be reported.

aware_at.description: When the manufacturer became aware (the clock for the 24-hour and 72-hour deadlines starts here), ISO 8601 with time zone, e.g. 2026-11-16T10:00:00Z. If unsure, use the earliest plausible time.

event_type.description: What happened: an actively exploited vulnerability in the product (evidence that an attacker has exploited it), or a severe incident having an impact on the security of the product.

fix_available_at.description: Vulnerabilities only: when a corrective or mitigating measure (patch, security update, fix) became available (ISO 8601 with zone).

notification_submitted_at.description: Severe incidents only: when the 72-hour notification was submitted (ISO 8601 with zone).

name: cra_reporting_deadlines
title: Compute CRA Article 14 reporting deadlines
